aboutPreview.bio: Josué Cabrera (Mexico City, 1986). Performing artist, theatre and popular-dance teacher, cook, and developer. As you can probably tell, he doesn't know how to sit still, which has led him to move around and try living in different places: born in the former Federal District, he arrived in Ciudad Neza at one year old and grew up there. As an adult —yes, supposedly— he moved to Tláhuac and later to the Narvarte neighborhood in present-day Mexico City. Later he moved to Yucatán to sample the sweetness of Mérida, and when it wasn't quite so sweet, he relocated to Chelem, a municipality of Progreso. Near the end of the COVID-19 pandemic, by a stroke of luck, he arrived in Puerto Morelos, Quintana Roo, where he managed three moves in a single year within the same charming town.

acting.title: ACTING
acting.subtitle: Here and now.
acting.description: My first contact with theatre was through acting. I started in workshops wanting to become an actor, though what I really wanted was to be a mime and clown. Then, you know, life led me down the wrong path —or maybe not. My nature kept asking me to diversify. I don't know whether that's good or bad; it's simply how it is... so I'm always open to whatever I'm invited to do...
acting.imageAlt: Josué Cabrera durante un trabajo como actor

directing.title: DIRECTING
directing.subtitle: Looking from the outside. Though never entirely.
directing.description: After being far from home and from the people I had always teamed up with, or who used to invite me into their projects, I found myself needing to experiment, mess things up, and make discoveries from this complex role.
directing.imageAlt: Josué Cabrera. Dirección de Tlaloques, extranjeros y otros mensajeros

dramaturgy.title: PLAYWRITING
dramaturgy.subtitle: Words get stuck in my throat.
dramaturgy.description: Putting what I feel onto paper is a relatively recent process for me. Even though I had written before, I had never allowed myself to do it in a more formal, structured, and consistent way. During the pandemic I began my first text that would make it to the stage, initially by intuition. Later I felt the need to continue these processes, so I began taking workshops guided by admirable people whom I am fortunate to call my teachers.
dramaturgy.imageAlt: Proceso de escritura y dramaturgia de Josué Cabrera

hero.description: I'm not interested in answers. I'm interested in creating spaces where we can ask better questions.
hero.imageAlt: Josué Cabrera durante un proceso pedagógico

manifesto.text: My pedagogical practice comes from theatre, improvisation, and dance. I'm interested in creating spaces where learning is not only about acquiring a technique, but about listening, playing, making mistakes, building with others, and finding one's own tools.

forum.title: FORUM THEATRE
forum.subtitle: The stage as a space to rehearse other possibilities.
forum.description: Forum Theatre allows us to look at a conflict, intervene in it, and collectively build questions about our reality. It is a practice in which those watching can also step onto the stage and propose other paths.

improv.title: NOT KNOWING WHAT WILL HAPPEN CAN BE TRAINED TOO.

training.description: Supporting teacher training means going beyond teaching steps: observing how a technique is transmitted, how a process is accompanied, and how tools are built so that each teacher can find their own way of teaching.
